match.reason: The bank point teaches the balance sheet and owner's equity in general, not carrying amount, depreciation or its treatment in the income statement, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Carrying amount
card: Accumulated depreciation is the total depreciation charged on an asset since it was bought. It grows each year the asset is used.
Carrying amount = cost less accumulated depreciation. It is the part of the asset's cost not yet written off as an expense.
Each year's depreciation is an expense in the income statement. It lowers profit for that year.
The carrying amount is reported in the balance sheet, under non-current assets. It falls each year as accumulated depreciation grows.
draft.remember: Depreciation goes in the income statement. Carrying amount goes in the balance sheet.

a.q: Which of these is the carrying amount of an asset?
opts: Cost less accumulated depreciation
Cost plus accumulated depreciation
The depreciation expense for the latest year
The price the asset could be sold for today
a.why: Carrying amount is what is left of the cost after the total depreciation so far is taken off. The latest year's expense is only one year of depreciation, not the total, so it is not the carrying amount.
a.clue: Think of cost with the total depreciation so far taken off.

b.q: Priya's Bakery in Ballarat bought an oven for $24 000. After three years its accumulated depreciation is $9 000. Where is the $15 000 shown?
opts: In the balance sheet, as the oven's carrying amount
In the income statement, as the oven's carrying amount
In the income statement, as a depreciation expense
In the balance sheet, as accumulated depreciation
b.why: $24 000 less $9 000 is $15 000, which is the carrying amount, and carrying amount is shown in the balance sheet. Accumulated depreciation is the $9 000, not the $15 000.
b.clue: Work out cost less accumulated depreciation first.

b.best: In the balance sheet, as the oven's carrying amount

problems.detail: The clue ('Think of cost with the total depreciation so far taken off') restates the right option almost word for word. A student could match it without knowing what carrying amount is.
